title: GEM: An implementation of the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation for simulating interacting quantum systems
authors: Samuele Giuli, Tsung-Han Lee, Yong-Xin Yao, Ina Park, Harrison LaBollita, Ivan Pasqua, Nicola Lanatà, Olivier Gingras
abstract: We present GEM (Ghost Embedding Method), an open-source software package written in Python for computing equilibrium properties of strongly correlated electronic systems within the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation method. GEM provides a computationally efficient framework for studying multi-orbital lattice models. It supports zero- and finite-temperature calculations and symmetry broken phases. It is integrated with the TRIQS ecosystem, providing tools for model construction, self-consistent solution, and evaluation of physical observables. We first detail the method's theoretical formulation, then we present the software architecture, and finally we introduce some practical workflow, which also validates the implementation against established results. In particular, we illustrate the capabilities of GEM through multiorbital and finite-temperature applications and discuss its computational cost relative to more demanding quantum embedding approaches.
summary: This paper introduces GEM, a new open-source Python package implementing the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation for simulating strongly correlated electronic systems. It provides a computationally efficient method to calculate equilibrium properties for multi-orbital lattice models. By systematically bridging the gap between simpler approximations and full DMFT, GEM offers a powerful, versatile tool for condensed matter theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of computing equilibrium properties for strongly correlated electronic systems, which are notoriously difficult to model accurately.
main_result: The authors introduce GEM, an open-source Python package that provides a computationally efficient framework for studying multi-orbital lattice models using the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation.
method: The method employs the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation, which is formulated via a free-energy functional that systematically bridges the gap between static Gutzwiller approximations and fully dynamical DMFT.
model_or_system: The focus is on general multi-orbital lattice models, described by a Hamiltonian containing hopping terms and local interaction terms, analogous to the Hubbard model.
key_observables: Equilibrium properties, total energy, free energy, static expectation values (order parameters), and spectral function features.
important_parameters: The number of auxiliary bath modes ($B$), which controls the approximation level; zero- and finite-temperature regimes.
main_assumptions: The core approximation is the ghost-Gutzwiller treatment, which simplifies the self-consistency cycle by using thermal one-body density matrices instead of full Green's functions.
figures_summary: The notes describe a four-step iterative self-consistency cycle involving solving Hamiltonians ($\hat{H}_{qp}, \hat{H}_i^{	ext{emb}}$) and updating parameters ($\Delta_i, \Sigma_i$) to match thermal one-body density matrices.
paper_structure: The paper first details the theoretical formulation of the ghost-GA functional, then presents the software architecture of the GEM package, and finally illustrates the practical workflow with validation against established results.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the systematic, controlled approximation scheme (controlled by $B$) and the integration with established computational ecosystems (TRIQS) offer valuable lessons in developing scalable numerical tools for complex quantum many-body problems.
